rationale: Start with a broad mid-temperature scouting gradient to ensure all 8 compounds elute within 42 min and reveal the overall elution window and any critical pairs. This gives a balanced first map of retention without being so steep that everything compresses into the dead time.

If the critical pair responds strongly, we can then shorten and trim; if not, we will know to use temperature or window shifts instead.

This should retain the strong selectivity gain seen at 40 min while reducing the time penalty enough to improve CRF over the 40 min run.

The broad-window results show slope alone trades one critical pair against another, so temperature is the next lever for selectivity. A 15 C drop should increase retention modestly and may reorder or separate the close pairs while keeping the last peak likely near the 10 min target.
